hints: The list is sorted, so where do all copies of the same value sit relative to each other?
One pointer walk: because equal values are adjacent, compare each node with its next. If they match, unlink the next node; otherwise move forward.

1. Set cur = head.
  2. While cur != null and cur.next != null:
  3. If cur.next.val == cur.val, set cur.next = cur.next.next (stay on cur).
  4. Otherwise move cur = cur.next.
  5. Return head.

approaches.name: Set of seen values
approaches.idea: Track seen values in a set and skip repeats. Works even unsorted, but uses memory.

approaches.name: Optimal: compare with the next node
approaches.idea: Sorted order puts duplicates side by side.

explain: For 2→2→3→5→5→5→8: at the first 2 we drop the second 2; at 3 nothing; at 5 we drop two 5s one after the other, staying on the first 5 each time; then 8. The result is 2→3→5→8. Not advancing after an unlink is important, otherwise a run of three equal values would leave one behind. An empty list returns null.
recognize: Remove duplicates from a sorted list → duplicates are adjacent, so compare each node with the next.
javascript: function deleteDuplicates(head) { const a = []; for (let c = head; c; c = c.next) if (!a.length || a[a.length-1].val !== c.val) a.push(c); for (let i = 0; i < a.length; i++) a[i].next = a[i+1] || null; return a[0] || null; }
